audit.report: A batch_replayable_inventory worker (pid 326875) held an idle-in-transaction state for 4.1 seconds, blocking checkout and causing 4 timeouts in 15 seconds (92% success, below the 95% SLO). The business federation was down, making workload registry, change calendar, and biz.tradeoff data unavailable, so neither guardian could confirm replayability or tolerated degradation. After three rounds of proposing to wait, the Database Guardian escalated when the blocker did not clear. The Continuity Guardian accepted escalation because required tradeoff evidence was missing. No automated action executed; the incident was handed to on-call at 110.4 seconds.
audit.root_cause: A batch_replayable_inventory transaction (pid 326875) remained idle in transaction for 4.1s, blocking checkout and degrading success to 92% while business context services were unreachable.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory workload: add a local fallback interrupt policy (max idle-in-transaction TTL) so the Database Guardian can act without biz.tradeoff when the federation is down.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian repeated the same wait proposal for three rounds without new evidence that the blocker would clear, wasting two rounds; the Continuity Guardian correctly held on invariant I7 (missing biz.tradeoff) but could not force a safer action because escalation was the only remaining option.
follow_ups: Implement a configurable idle-in-transaction killer for batch_replayable_inventory workers with a default 5s TTL.
Deploy a cached copy of workload registry and change calendar to the database guardian's local store with a 5-minute TTL.
Add checkout client-side latency and error-rate metrics to the database telemetry stream so SLO breach is visible without biz.impact.
